raw_response:
I farm the way I know best: I keep the land split between cash income and grain for the household. Since I have 10.9 mu, well irrigation, and a long habit of managing cotton together with grain, I will put 6.0 mu into cotton as my main cash crop, and I will keep 4.9 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps stand establishment and yield, but I will not push inputs too hard because I want to control cost and labor. Cotton gets the most careful fertilizer and pest management because it brings in cash but also carries more risk. Wheat and maize are steadier, and with irrigation I can support them with moderate fertilizer and a few timely waterings. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it fits my scale, my labor situation, and the way I already manage residues and seedbeds.
